title: Redwood All-Hands - March 2027
summary: Monthly all-hands: product update, 2027 Q1 progress vs goals, reliability/infra wins, hiring and org changes, roadmap highlights, security/compliance update, and company metrics. Q&A at end. Deck and recording linked.

transcript:
Header:
Date: 2027-03-15 10:00 PT / 17:00 UTC
Duration: ~75 minutes
Location: All-hands (Zoom) - Recorded
Attendees: company-wide (~150), remote offices NA/EMEA/APAC
Links: Slides: https://redwood.com/slides/q1-2027-all-hands | Recording: posted after processing

Summary (auto-gen, short): Product and infra wins this quarter, continued ARR growth, Dedicated momentum with two new pilots, SOC 2 continuous monitoring on track, hiring ramp across infra and sales. Q&A at end.

00:00 Alex: Hey everyone, thanks for joining, seems like we have folks from London to Seoul, uh welcome to the March all-hands. Quick agenda: metrics, product updates from Priya and Marcus, security from Lena + special shoutouts, then Q&A.

01:05 Alex: Ok first, metrics - revenue and adoption. We closed a couple of mid-market pilots this quarter and ARR growth is holding at +28% Y/Y, churn unchanged, logo expansion is improving. Not perfect but solid runway. There's some noise from cloud costs but we'll talk cost controls later.

03:12 Priya: Thanks Alex. Quick infra highlights - we've shipped a kernel-selection optimizer that reduced p99 generation latency by ~12% on average for the path we tested, and combined with smarter KV cache warmups we've seen up to 25% token cost reduction for customer workloads with high prefix reuse. Note these are workload dependent, so please see the benchmark sheet.

04:40 Marcus: I can add to that - engineering did a targeted pass on batching heuristics and continuous batching schedulers. We rolled canary to Dedicated earlier this week, early signals look good - throughput up ~18% at 50ms tail targets. There were a couple of regressions on small sequence workloads, we flagged and hotfixed last night.

06:05 Alex: Nice. On product: Redwood API got a small release - streaming stability improvements and better function calling edge cases, and Redwood Console now shows token-level cost breakdowns per route in beta. We'll roll that wider in two weeks.

08:20 Lena: Security and compliance - SOC 2 continuous monitoring beta is live for customers on Dedicated and Private; integration with KMS and HSM for key custody is progressing, we shipped the first PoC for a financial services customer requesting FIPS-backed HSMs. On SSO: new SCIM provisioning improvements are in place with Okta and Azure. Audit logs export format updated per customer feedback.

10:35 Alex: Customer wins - two Dedicated pilots signed (one fintech, one e-commerce), and a private on-prem pilot for a health care provider is scheduled to start next month. The health-care customer has stricter data residency and we are doing an air-gapped deployment with our on-prem package. Big shoutout to the SE and Solutions team for the rapid scoping.

13:05 Priya: A few notes on model catalog & serving: we've added three new open models with verified performance profiles and recommended quantization knobs. The runtime now auto-selects kernels based on observed sequence length distributions, though please remember it's still a heuristic and we provide toggles in the config.

15:40 Marcus: Ops and reliability - overall uptime last month 99.92% across hosted infra, Dedicated SLA runbooks updated, incident post-mortems are on the ops page. We are pushing a new tracer that captures KV cache hit ratios; early visibility is already helping customers who had unexpected cold-start costs.

18:01 Alex: People update - hiring ramp approved for infra (+8 engineers), sales (+5 AE/CS), and security (+2). We still have gaps in ML infra and QA, managers please nudge recruiting. Also reorganizing product slightly: consolidating serving runtime and kernel teams under Marcus to speed decision cycles.

20:30 Lena: A note on internal policies - remote-first still, but we will pilot monthly in-person hubs in SF and Amsterdam for team syncs. Expense policy updated for travel - check People Ops.

22:00 Alex: Financials - burn is lower than plan as of Feb; runway extended by 6 months vs forecast given better-than-expected renewals. Still conservative on hiring if we see materially higher cloud costs.

24:15 Speaker 1 (Emily, Eng): Quick question - on the kernel selection, is there a way for SEs to force a kernel override per customer to avoid fallback during pilots?

24:45 Marcus: Yes, we have a config toggle in the runtime and an admin flag in Dedicated; we'll share a short how-to doc. Action: Marcus to post the override doc.

26:20 Speaker 2 (Raj, Solutions): One more on the health-care pilot - do we have a compliance checklist for air-gapped installs, like audit log retention and KMS options?

27:00 Lena: Good question, Raj - yes, there is a checklist. We'll attach the initial version to the pilot ticket and share wider. We've also started documenting required approvals for on-prem builds.

29:10 Alex: Quick customer story - a retail customer reduced per-session token cost by ~17% when switching to our Recommended batching + KV cache profile; they also reported better latency consistency during peak sale events.

31:05 Priya: Roadmap highlights - next quarter: 1) Redwood Optimize private beta (focus on automated quantization recommendations and batching profiles), 2) broader rollout of per-route token cost in Console, 3) improved model fallbacks for graceful degradation across regions. We're aiming to open Optimize beta to customers mid-April.

34:30 Alex: Go-to-market - PLG signals remain strong, we shipped new quickstarts for common frameworks and an SDK update that simplifies streaming + function calls. Enterprise sales: tightened our Dedicated pricing tiers and introduced burst credits for seasonal workloads.

36:50 Marcus: Technical deep dive teaser - next Tuesday we'll host an internal deep dive on continuous batching heuristics and kernel selection, engineers encouraged to join. Link will be posted.

38:15 Speaker 3 (Tara, Sales): Any change to the renewal playbooks for Dedicated customers with pilots going to production?

38:40 Alex: Not materially - playbooks updated with new SLA language and cost controls; Sales Ops will publish an FAQ.

40:00 Q&A begins, folks dropping in audio - occasional crosstalk, some transcription noise.

42:30 Speaker 4 (Mike, Finance): On cloud cost controls - what are the immediate levers to reduce variable GPU spend?

43:00 Priya: Short term: adjust batching window and prefix caching TTLs, enable quantized models where customers can accept a small quality delta, route lower-priority traffic to cheaper model variants. Ops can throttle non-critical background workloads. Longer term: better spot-instance scheduling and model compilation for cheaper inference.

45:20 Speaker 1 (Emily): For the model quantization recommendations, can we get an internal guide?

45:40 Product team: Yes, we'll publish a guide - product to own it and link from the Console.

48:00 Alex: Recognition time - kudos to the infra team for on-call rotation improvements and to Solutions for closing the health-care pilot RFI so quickly.

50:10 Lena: Compliance quick update - one external audit scheduled, and SOC 2 rescan for Dedicated customers next quarter; we'll publish timelines.

52:20 Marcus: Small technical note - we identified an edge-case where long conversation contexts with heavy function calls could build up KV cache memory. We put a guard in place; will run memtests next week.

54:00 Speaker 5 (Nina, Product): Roadmap question - Optimize private beta, will customers be able to see per-prompt recommendations?

54:25 Priya: Yes, the plan is to surface per-prompt batching and quantization suggestions as part of the beta; however initially it's internal-only to validate.

56:00 Alex: Ok let's wrap - recap of next steps: slides + recording posted, Marcus to publish latency benchmark, Product to send beta invite form, People Ops to update headcount plan.

58:10 Alex: Open mic - a few quick shoutouts, then we'll end.

70:00 End of recording.

Notes on transcript quality: medium - live meeting, multiple speakers, some crosstalk, transcription mis-heard a few proper nouns (e.g., HSM variant typed as 'H-S-M' sometimes), timestamps approximate.
